 Judgement
The Sub-Inspector of Banashankari Traffic Police Station has filed the charge sheet against the
accused No.1 for the offences punishable U/s.279 and 338 of Ipc, Sec.134(a and b) R/w.187 of
M.V.Act and against the accused No.2 for the offences punishable U/s.146 R/w.196 and Sec.66(1)
R/w.192 of M.V.Act.
2. It is the case of the prosecution that on 28-10-2020 at about 7.00 p.m. the 1st accused being the
driver Auto Rickshaw bearing registration No.KA- 05/Ab-1263 drove the same on K.R. Road, from
Bharathi Nursing home junction towards Upahara Sagar hotel junction in a rash and negligent
manner C.C.No.202/2021 so as to endanger human life and he dashed to pedestrian who was
crossing the K.R. Road, in front of Mtr Food store, from Umamehshwara adyatma Manidra
towards Mtr food store. Due to the impact the pedestrian C.W.5 Sri Ramprasad N.A., aged about
52 years sustained grievous injuries. Further on the day of accident the accused No.1 did not provide
medical aid to the injured nor he intimated the police about. Further on the day of accident the 2nd
accused being the owner of the Auto Rickshaw bearing registration No.KA-05/AB-1263 had
permitted the accused No.1 to drive the said vehicle and the said vehicle was not in possession of
valid vehicle insurance and fitness certificate on the day of accident , thereby the accused No.1 is
alleged to have committed the offence punishable U/s.279 and 338 of Ipc, Sec.134(a & b) R/w.187
of M.V.Act and the 2nd accused is alleged to have committed the offence punishable U/s.66(1)
R/w.192 and Sec.146 R/w.196 of M.V.Act.
3. Upon taking cognizance, case came to be registered against the accused No.1 for the offences
C.C.No.202/2021 punishable U/s.279 and 338 of Ipc, Sec.134(a & b) R/w.187 of Mv Act and the
accused No.2 for the offences punishable U/s.66(1) R/w.192 and Sec.146 appeared before the court
through their counsel and got enlarged on bail. Charge sheet copies furnished to the accused
persons and thereby provision U/s.207 of Cr.P.C. duly complied with. 
4. Plea came to be framed for the offences U/s.279 and 338 of Ipc, Sec.134(a & b) R/w.187,
Sec.66(1) R/w.192 and Sec.146 R/w.196 of M.V.Act. for which accused No.1 and 2 have pleaded not
guilty claimed to be tried. 
5. During the course of trial, the prosecution has examined P.W.1 to 8 and got marked documents as
per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.9. On completion of prosecution side evidence, the statement of accused U/s.313
of denied all the incriminating evidence appearing against them. 
6. Heard both the sides. The learned App argued that in the instant case the eye witness P.W.2, 3
and C.C.No.202/2021 4 who have witnessed the incident has supported the case of the prosecution
and their evidence is corroborated by the evidence of investigating officer. In the case on hand the
prosecution has proved its case and accordingly prays for conviction. To counter the said argument
the learned counsel for the accused submits that in the instant case the injured is the manager in the
temple. The said fact is disclosed by his wife in his complaint itself. The prosecution examined
P.W.2 to 5 among them Pw..2 is the street vendor opposite to temple, P.W.3 is the watchman of the

With regard to P.W.1 the counsel contended that in her complaint she has stated she has received
information about accident from general public, prosecution listed out three employees of the
temple as witness and the injured was taken to hospital by temple authority then how come general
C.C.No.202/2021 public intimate her. This shows there is a conspiracy against accused persons. He
further contended that the prosecution claims negligence on the part of the accused. As per the
sketch map produced by Io the injured was not proceeding in footpath and the alleged incident has
taken place in the center of the road. There is no mention of existence of any zebra cross near
accident spot and the path way shown by the investigating officer is not a straight lane which means
contributory negligence on the part of the injured is clearly noticeable. The said fact is admitted by
two eye witnesses as well in their cross- examination. 
7. He further argued that as per the version of the prosecution one Yoga Narasimha who is the
relative of the injured taken the injured to hospital, but in wound certificate there is no mention
about his name as per witness the injured has taken two days treatment in hospital, but there is no
mention about the same in charge sheet and prosecution did not obtain any certificate from the
Digvijay hospital. The complainant claims the injured was admitted in hospital as in patient for 3
months. To support the C.C.No.202/2021 said contention no document is produced before the
court. P.W.1 claims her husband is working in the said temple where accident has taken place, but
she did not mention anybody's name in her complaint and claims she received information from
general public. The same is not tenable and it shows it is a coocked up story. Admittedly the accident
has taken place in a junction and there is no zebra cross which means pedestrians is at fault. The
prosecution did not establish the chain link between the eye witnesses, prosecution has not
examined any independent eye witnesses. Io claims about existence of cctv even the manager
admits about existence of cctv, but intentionally the said cctv footage is not produced before the
court which raises doubt about the case of the prosecution. The burden is upon the prosecution to
prove its case beyond reasonable doubt, but prosecution was not successful in establishing the
negligent act of the accused. In the case on hand though the victim is listed as witness he was not
examined and the reason assigned is mental illness. To support the said contention no medical
record is placed before the court, it is not C.C.No.202/2021 tenable in the court of law a person can
do acting and court can accept his version. Here the burden is upon the prosecution to prove the
mental condition by relevant documents which they failed to do so. Upon perusal of the over all
evidence the prosecution is not successful in establishing their case of negligence. Accordingly he
prays for acquittal of accused. 
8. The points that arise for my determination are as under:

Nursing home junction towards Upahara Sagar hotel junction in a rash and negligent
manner so as to endanger human life, thereby the 1st accused committed offence

In the instant case the prosecution is alleging that the accused being the driver of the auto rickshaw drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and caused accident due to which the victim sustained grievous injuries and prosecution contended that accused committed the offences punishable U/s.279, 338 of IPC. Section 279 IPC deals with rash and negligent driving of any vehicle or riding on a public way in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life or likely to cause hurt or injury to any person. In order to constitute an offence U/s.279 of IPC, it must be established that the accused was driving the vehicle on a public way in rash and negligent manner to endanger human life or to likely cause to hurt or injury to any other person. For the purpose of section 279 rash and negligent may be described as criminal C.C.No.202/2021 rashness or criminal negligence. It must be more than mere carelessness of error of judgment. The essential ingredients of section 279 are: (1) rash and negligent driving or riding on a public way, (ii) The act must be such as to endanger human life or likely to cause hurt or injury to any person.
